text:
Situation: Diltiazem hydrochloride is not on FDA's current shortage list as of 2026-10-21. FDA's history shows an earlier shortage first posted on 2018-02-21, since resolved. Current stock at Corvale East shows 9.3 days for 100 mg and 23 days for 240 mg capsules. Corvale General holds 20.9 days for 100 mg injection, 19.7 days for 240 mg injection, and 18.8 days for 5 mg/mL.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 976095 at Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 623 days before the 2018-02-21 shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 372 days before the shortage posting. A later FDA inspection 1064827 at the plant ended 2018-08-15 and was classified OAI, 175 days after the shortage posting. FDA lists the Hospira 100 mg/1 product as To Be Discontinued (posted 2026-01-05).

Our position: Corvale East 100 mg supply is below target. Corvale General can support a transfer. Alternative manufacturers are not on FDA's shortage list. The Hospira 100 mg/1 product is flagged for discontinuation.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 50 vials of 100 mg from Corvale General to Corvale East — approved by pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. Buy from Sagent Pharmaceuticals — approved by buyer.
3. Buy from WG Critical Care, LLC — approved by buyer.
4. Use Diltiazem Hydrochloride 5 mg/mL from Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. — pharmacist verification required; approved by Casey Nguyen, MD on 2026-06-27.
5. Use DILTIAZEM HYDROCHLORIDE 100 mg/1 from Hospira, Inc. — pharmacist verification required; approved by Sam Rivera, MD on 2025-12-18; note FDA To Be Discontinued status posted 2026-01-05.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or therapeutic substitutions; those are for treating clinicians and the committee.
